steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Functionalism (Durkheim, Parsons): society is a system of interdependent parts working together to maintain stability. Each institution has a function: family socialises children, education teaches skills, economy provides material needs. Society is based on value consensus (shared norms and values). | Key Fact: Marxism (Marx, Engels): society is divided by class conflict between the bourgeoisie (owners of production) and proletariat (workers). The ruling class controls the economy and ideology (institutions like education and media maintain ruling class dominance). Capitalism exploits workers and creates false consciousness (workers accept a system that exploits them). | Key Fact: Feminism (Oakley, Barrett): society is patriarchal (male-dominated). Liberal feminism seeks reform

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Compare Functionalism and Marxism as sociological perspectives. | Explain how Feminism challenges traditional sociological perspectives. | Evaluate whether Interactionism provides a more valid view of society than Functionalism.
